name: libkeyfinder
desc: Musical key detection for digital audio, GPL v3
why: Detects the musical key of audio using signal analysis, a real transform from sound to music theory, though it is a library.

brief.what_it_is: libkeyfinder is a small C++11 library that estimates the musical key of digital audio. You give it audio samples with a frame rate and channel count, and it returns a key value (a KeyFinder::key_t) for the whole track. It can also run in progressive mode, where it builds a chromagram from a stream of audio packets and reports key estimates as it goes. It is a library with no standalone GUI in this repo. The GUI app by the original author is separate and no longer maintained.
brief.why_it_exists: It was written by Ibrahim Shaath in 2011 as part of a master's thesis in computer science, and in 2020 maintenance passed to the Mixxx DJ software team, who incorporated it into Mixxx as of Mixxx 2.3. The README frames it as a reusable key-detection component for audio software.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the signal-processing method in detail. It says the library turns audio into a chromatic representation (a chromagram) and estimates key from that. The progressive API lets a caller feed packets and read the most recent key estimate, then call finalChromagram for a final result. The README links the thesis, 'Estimations of key in digital music recordings', for the underlying method.

commands_seen.context: Debian/Ubuntu: installs CMake and the FFTW3 development headers, a dependency the library needs.
macOS via Homebrew: installs the build tools and FFTW3 and Catch2 dependencies.
Configures the build from the repo top level into a build directory, with a chosen install prefix.
Compiles the library in the build directory, using the given number of parallel jobs.
Installs the built library to the prefix set at configure time.
Same configure step as above; add -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF to build a static library instead.
Runs the test suite from the build directory. The README warns that FftAdapterTest/ForwardAndBackward fails intermittently.
macOS: prints the logical CPU count to use for the --parallel flag.

brief.install_notes: Needs FFTW3 installed first (the README lists per-platform packages: dnf, apt, pacman, brew, vcpkg). Needs CMake. Catch2 is only needed for the tests; if it is missing, CMake downloads it automatically. To skip tests, pass -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF. Windows install uses 'vcpkg install fftw3 catch2'. Typical macOS install prefix is /usr/local. No accounts or runtime setup are mentioned.
brief.standout: The library has a real transform from audio to music theory with a documented API, and it has been carried on by a DJ software team rather than left to rot. Its progressive chromagram mode lets a host read key estimates while audio is still streaming.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the evidence shows. The README says the Mixxx team took over maintenance in 2020, invites pull requests and issues on GitHub, and has a build status badge pointing to a GitHub Actions workflow. I did not see a release date or a last commit date in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm recent activity beyond that.
brief.caveats: The GUI application is no longer maintained and does not build on contemporary Linux distributions. Building requires FFTW3 and CMake. The README notes an intermittent test failure in FftAdapterTest/ForwardAndBackward. The README gives no license detail beyond GPL v3 or later. I did not see the thesis or any accuracy benchmarks.
quotes: A small C++11 library for estimating the musical key of digital audio.
libkeyfinder is a small C++11 library for estimating the musical key of digital audio. It is published under the GNU General Public License (GPL) version 3 or later.
In 2020, Ibrahim handed over maintenance of libkeyfinder to the Mixxx DJ software team who incorporated it into Mixxx as of Mixxx 2.3.
